items.stem: From a point T outside a circle of centre O, tangents TP and TQ are drawn to the circle. Prove that OT is the right bisector of line segment PQ.
items.answer:
Let OT cut the chord PQ at R.
Since the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal, TP = TQ, so ΔTPQ is isosceles and its base angles are equal: ∠TPR = ∠TQR.
Now compare ΔPTR and ΔQTR:
TP = TQ, TR = TR (common) and ∠TPR = ∠TQR.
Hence ΔPTR ≅ ΔQTR, and by CPCT PR = QR and ∠PRT = ∠QRT.
But PQ is a straight line, so ∠PRT + ∠QRT = 180°, which gives ∠PRT = ∠QRT = 90°.
So TR (that is, OT) both bisects PQ and is perpendicular to it. Therefore OT is the right bisector of PQ. Hence proved.

items.stem: In Figure, PQ and RS are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O and another tangent AB with point of contact C intersecting PQ at A and RS at B. Prove that ∠AOB = 90°.
items.answer:
Let PQ touch the circle at D and RS touch it at E. Because PQ ∥ RS and both are tangents, D, O and E are collinear, so DOE is a straight line.
In ΔDOA and ΔCOA: DA = AC (tangents drawn from the common point A), OD = OC (radii), OA is common, and ∠ODA = ∠OCA = 90° because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
So ΔDOA ≅ ΔCOA, and by CPCT ∠DOA = ∠COA.  …(1)
In the same way ΔBOC ≅ ΔBOE gives ∠COB = ∠BOE.  …(2)
The angles at O along the straight line DOE add to 180°:
∠DOA + ∠AOC + ∠COB + ∠BOE = 180°
Using (1) and (2), 2∠AOC + 2∠COB = 180°, so ∠AOC + ∠COB = 90°.
That sum is exactly ∠AOB. Therefore ∠AOB = 90°. Hence proved.

items.stem: Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
items.answer:
Let ABCD be a parallelogram circumscribing a circle, touching AB at P, BC at Q, CD at R and DA at S.
Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB = CD and AD = BC.  …(1)
The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point are equal, so
at A: AP = AS,  at B: BP = BQ,  at C: CR = CQ,  at D: DR = DS.
Adding these four equalities,
AP + PB + CR + DR = AS + BQ + CQ + DS
Grouping the pieces along each side gives AB + CD = AD + BC.
Using (1), 2AB = 2AD, so AB = AD.
A parallelogram with two adjacent sides equal has all four sides equal. Therefore ABCD is a rhombus. Hence proved.

items.stem: In given figure, PA and PB are tangents from a point P to the circle with centre O. At the point M, other tangent to the circle is drawn cutting PA and PB at K and N. Prove that the perimeter of ΔPNK = 2PB.
items.answer:
Tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal in length, so
PA = PB (from P), KM = KA (from K) and MN = BN (from N).
Now KN = KM + MN = KA + BN.
The perimeter of ΔPNK is
p = PN + KN + PK
 = PN + BN + KA + PK
 = (PN + NB) + (PK + KA)
 = PB + PA
 = 2PB, since PA = PB.
Therefore the perimeter of ΔPNK = 2PB. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the figure, tangents PQ and PR are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O, such that ∠RPQ = 30°. A chord RS is drawn parallel to the tangent PQ. Find ∠RQS.
items.answer:
Tangents from an external point are equal, so PR = PQ and ΔPQR is isosceles.
Its base angles are therefore equal:
∠PRQ = ∠PQR = (180° − 30°)/2 = 150°/2 = 75°
Since SR ∥ QP, the angles ∠SRQ and ∠RQP are alternate angles, so
∠SRQ = ∠RQP = 75°
In ΔSQR this makes SQ = RQ, so the angles opposite them are equal:
∠RSQ = ∠SRQ = 75°
By the angle sum of ΔSQR,
∠SQR + 75° + 75° = 180°
∠SQR = 180° − 150° = 30°
Therefore ∠RQS = 30°.

items.stem: In the figure AB and CD are common tangents to two circles of unequal radii. Prove that AB = CD.
items.answer:
Extend AB and CD so that they meet at a point P; they do meet because the two circles have unequal radii.
From the external point P, PA and PC are tangents to the larger circle, so
PA = PC
Also from P, PB and PD are tangents to the smaller circle, so
PB = PD
Subtracting the second equality from the first,
PA − PB = PC − PD
But PA − PB = AB and PC − PD = CD.
Therefore AB = CD. Hence proved.

items.stem: In figure PQ is a tangent from an external point P to a circle with centre O and OP cuts the circle at T and ∠QOR is a diameter. If ∠POR = 130° and S is a point on the circle, find ∠1 + ∠2.
items.answer:
A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠OQP = 90°.
T lies on OP, so the central angle standing on arc TR is ∠TOR = ∠POR = 130°.
The angle subtended at the centre is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc, so at S
∠2 = ½ ∠TOR = ½ ∠POR = ½ × 130° = 65°
QOR is a diameter, so ∠QOR = 180° and
∠POQ = 180° − 130° = 50°
In ΔOQP the angles add to 180°:
∠1 = 180° − ∠OQP − ∠POQ = 180° − 90° − 50° = 40°
Therefore ∠1 + ∠2 = 65° + 40° = 105°.

items.stem: In the given figure, AD is a diameter of a circle with centre O and AB is a tangent at A. C is a point on the circle such that DC produced intersects the tangent at B and ∠ABC = 50°. Find ∠AOC.
items.answer:
A tangent drawn at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact, so at A
∠A = ∠OAB = 90°
In ΔDAB the angles add to 180°:
∠D + ∠A + ∠B = 180°
∠D + 90° + 50° = 180°
∠D = 40°
The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle it subtends at the circumference, and ∠ADC = ∠D stands on arc AC. So
∠AOC = 2∠ADC = 2 × 40° = 80°
Therefore ∠AOC = 80°.

items.stem: In the given figure, PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. CD is another tangent touching the circle at Q. If PA = 12 cm, QC = QD = 3 cm, then find PC + PD.
items.answer:
Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length, so
from C: CA = CQ = 3 cm
from D: DQ = DB = 3 cm
from P: PB = PA = 12 cm
Writing each of PA and PB in two pieces,
PA + PB = (PC + CA) + (PD + DB)
so PC + PD = PA − CA + PB − DB
 = 12 − 3 + 12 − 3
 = 18 cm
Therefore PC + PD = 18 cm.

items.stem:
A backyard is in the shape of a triangle ABC with right angle at B. AB = 7 m and BC = 15 m. A circular pit was dug inside it such that it touches the walls AC, BC and AB at P, Q and R respectively such that AP = x m.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:
(i) Find the length of AR in terms of x.
(ii) Write the type of quadrilateral BQOR.
(iii) Find the length PC in terms of x and hence find the value of x.
(iv) Find x and hence find the radius r of circle.
items.answer:
(i) Tangents from an external point are equal, so from A: AR = AP = x m.
(ii) A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so OR ⊥ AB and OQ ⊥ BC. Hence ∠ORB = ∠OQB = ∠RBQ = 90°, and by the angle sum of a quadrilateral ∠QOR = 360° − 90° − 90° − 90° = 90°. Also OR = OQ, both radii. So BQOR is a square.
(iii) By Pythagoras, AC = √(AB² + BC²) = √(7² + 15²) = √274 units, so PC = AC − AP = (√274 − x) units.
Also AR = AP = x, so BR = BQ = 7 − x, and CQ = PC = 15 − (7 − x) = x + 8.
Hence AC = AP + PC = x + x + 8 = 2x + 8, giving √274 = 2x + 8.
(iv) x = (√274 − 8)/2 m.
Since BQOR is a square, r = BR = 7 − x = 7 − (√274 − 8)/2 = (22 − √274)/2 m.
So x = (√274 − 8)/2 m and the radius r = (22 − √274)/2 m.

items.stem:
The picture given below shows a circular mirror hanging on the wall with a cord. The diagram represents the mirror as a circle with centre O. AP and AQ are tangents to the circle at P and Q respectively such that AP = 30 cm and ∠PAQ = 60°.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Find the length PQ.
(ii) Find m∠POQ.
(iii) Find the length OA.
(iv) Find the radius of the mirror.
items.answer:
Let M be the point where AO meets PQ. AO bisects ∠PAQ and is the perpendicular bisector of the chord PQ, so ∠PAM = 30° and ∠AMP = 90°.
(i) In ΔPAM, sin 30° = PM/AP, so ½ = PM/30, giving PM = 15 cm and PQ = 2PM = 30 cm.
(ii) In quadrilateral APOQ, ∠OPA = ∠OQA = 90° because a radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so
∠POQ + ∠OQA + ∠QAP + ∠APO = 360°
∠POQ + 90° + 60° + 90° = 360°
∠POQ + 240° = 360°, so m∠POQ = 120°.
(iii) In right ΔOAP, ∠OAP = 30° and cos 30° = AP/OA, so √3/2 = 30/OA, giving OA = 20√3 cm.
(iv) The radius is OP. In right ΔOAP, tan 30° = OP/AP, so 1/√3 = OP/30, giving OP = 10√3 cm.
So PQ = 30 cm, m∠POQ = 120°, OA = 20√3 cm and the radius of the mirror is 10√3 cm.

items.stem:
A children's park is in the triangular shape as shown in Figure below. In the middle of the park, there is a circular region for younger children to play. It is fenced with three layers of wire. The radius of the circular region is 3 m.
Based on the above, answer the following questions:
(i) Find the perimeter (or circumference) of the circular region.
(ii) What is the total length of wire used?
(iii) What is the area of the circular region?
(iv) If BD = 6 m, DC = 9 m and ar(ΔABC) = 54 m², then find the length of sides AB and AC, respectively.
(v) Find the perimeter of ΔABC.
items.answer:
(i) Perimeter of the circular region = 2πr = 2π × 3 = 6π m.
(ii) The fence has three layers, so the total wire = 3 × 6π = 18π m.
(iii) Area of the circular region = πr² = π(3)² = 9π m².
(iv) Let the circle touch AB at F, BC at D and CA at E. Tangents from a point are equal, so BF = BD = 6 m, CE = CD = 9 m; let AF = AE = x m. Then AB = x + 6, BC = 6 + 9 = 15 and AC = x + 9.
Splitting ΔABC into ΔAOB, ΔBOC and ΔAOC, each of height r = 3 m,
54 = ½ AB × OF + ½ BC × OD + ½ AC × OE
54 = ½(6 + x)(3) + ½(6 + 9)(3) + ½(9 + x)(3)
54 = (3/2)[6 + x + 15 + 9 + x]
36 = 2x + 30, so x = 3.
Hence AB = x + 6 = 9 m and AC = x + 9 = 12 m.
(v) Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BC + AC = 9 + 15 + 12 = 36 m.
